title: What If You Could See Everyone's Real Mental Age?
tags: what if you could see everyone's real mental age
description:
Monday morning on the school bus, the girl you like sits down next to you. Above her head floats a glowing number: 41. And nobody else can see it.

Your dad is 12. Your little sister is 47. The strictest teacher in school is 9. Then you save your neighbor's baby from a babysitter who is six inside, and soon the whole town knows. Half the internet calls you a fake, so the biggest show on TV wants to settle it live, in front of twenty thousand people. But you can't unsee a number, and people can feel it when you treat them like one. The number that matters most is your own.

• Subjective age: Rubin, D. C. & Berntsen, D. (2006). People over forty feel 20% younger than their age: Subjective age across the lifespan. Psychonomic Bulletin & Review, 13(5), 776–780.
• Parentification: American Psychological Association, APA Dictionary of Psychology, "parentification".
• Prefrontal cortex: Cleveland Clinic, "Prefrontal Cortex"; Gogtay, N. et al. (2004). Dynamic mapping of human cortical development during childhood through early adulthood. PNAS, 101(21), 8174–8179 (NIMH brain imaging study).

This is a fictional animated story. Lena, Jonah, Mason, Ivy, Mrs. Hale, the lunch lady and everyone else in it are made up and do not depict real people. The TV show, its host, the action star and the rapper are fictional too. Nobody can really see a "mental age": the numbers are a story idea, not a psychological test. Voices were generated with ElevenLabs.

So… would YOU want to see everyone's real mental age? 👇

title: What if you could feel your crush body?
tags: what if you could feel any girl's body
what if you could feel what girls feel
what if you had a superpower
description:
What if you woke up on day one of college and could feel exactly what any girl around you was feeling? Every cramp, every chill, every headache, every flutter of a crush, in your own body.

The power only works inside the campus gate. Step outside and it goes silent. Inside, you feel six thousand girls at once, and you have to learn the rules before they cost you everything. Then one night at a party, you feel something that doesn't belong to a normal night out. You have minutes to decide what to do with the one thing you can feel that nobody else can.

An animated What If story about empathy, friendship, and noticing when someone is in trouble.

title: What If Clothes Disappeared for a Whole Year?
tags: what if everyone stopped wearing clothes
description:
At midnight, every thread on Earth turns to dust. Shirts, socks, curtains, flags, even your teddy bear. Plastic, rubber and foil survive. Fabric doesn't. For one whole year, 8 billion people have nothing to wear.

Hour one is embarrassing. By hour three nobody cares. Then winter comes, and things get serious. Firefighters can't walk into flames, surgeons can't operate, sunscreen sells out everywhere, and whole cities drive south. A trillion-dollar industry vanishes overnight. And then something strange happens: strangers start talking, neighbors share one heater, and a whole block ends up in bubble wrap, laughing.

So what are clothes really for?

title: What If You Had Gojo's Powers in Real Life?
tags: what if you had gojo's powers
description:
You wake up at 7:42 in the morning. Your ceiling fan rips out of the ceiling and falls straight at your face… and then it stops. It never lands.

Overnight, you got Satoru Gojo's powers: the Six Eyes, the Limitless, Infinity, Blue, Red, Hollow Purple and Unlimited Void. But there are no sorcerers here, no monsters and nobody to teach you. Just you, in the real world.

What would actually happen? You can't shower. Your doctor can't draw blood. Your landlord wants you out. Then come the men in grey suits, the drone outside your window, the tests… and the sniper waiting for the one moment you switch Infinity off.

Every fact about the powers follows the manga:
• Infinity: things slow down forever and never arrive. Only you can turn it off, and keeping it on nonstop would fry your brain without the Reverse Cursed Technique.
• Six Eyes: perception and near-perfect energy control. It isn't mind reading or seeing the future, and it never switches off.
• Blue pulls. Red pushes, but only with the Reverse Cursed Technique. Hollow Purple is an imaginary mass that erases everything in its path.
• Unlimited Void: infinite information. In Shibuya, Gojo used it for just 0.2 seconds.
The events of the story are fiction.

title: What If You Became Perfect Whenever Your Crush Was Watching? (41 Fights, 0 Losses)
tags: what if you became perfect whenever your crush was watching
what if your crush was watching
description:
What if you became perfect whenever your crush was watching… and went straight back to being the most feared guy in school the second she looked away?

At Dockside High, they call you Red. 41 fights. 0 losses. Even the teachers take the long way around your locker. Then the new girl, Maya, walks up in the middle of fight number 42 and asks you where room 12 is. And something switches.

From that second on, whenever Maya is watching, you're a perfect gentleman: polite, gentle, straight A's. The moment she looks away, you're Red again. She thinks you're the nicest boy in school. 900 students know better, and nobody dares to tell her. Then the boy she changed schools to get away from shows up with a perfect smile, and he works out your secret: while she's watching, your fist won't close. He has a plan for the Winter Formal on December 17, in front of both schools.

title: What If You Had To Share A Body With Your Crush?
I Could See Everyone's IQ. The Top Student Had a 91—I Had a 151 and Was Failing Stats
tags: what if you could see everyone's IQ
description:
The guy who set the curve had a 91 IQ. Ezra had a 151—and three F's in a row.

One Tuesday morning, Ezra Dunbar woke up able to see a glowing number over everyone's head. His mom: 108. His dad: 103. The cat: nothing. In the hallway mirror, his own read 151—top 0.1%. Then his phone buzzed: two stats quizzes below passing, and his financial aid under review. That afternoon, Spencer Kingsley—top of every class, every professor's favorite—waved an A+ in Ezra's face while the whole room laughed. Over Spencer's head, in red: 91.

Ezra had the horsepower. He'd just never done the work. So his mom dropped his phone in the cookie jar, and his best friend Rudy drilled him on fractions until one in the morning. Then Professor Lin announced the State Scholars Cup: 240 students, 31 colleges, one full scholarship worth about $78,000. Ezra raised his hand. Spencer laughed and named himself the benchmark. And in the front row of the final sat a man in a charcoal suit, checking his watch.

👉 Watch till the end — the final round comes down to twenty seconds and one button.
